title: Flashcards: Architectural Buildings and Sites
items: New flashcard deck in Architectural Sites, Proponents, & Styles: a picture of a building on the front, its name, architect or proponent, and year on the back. 434 cards, built from the Identify the Structure question bank.

Cards are spaced out like Anki: rate each one Again, Hard, Good or Easy, and missed cards come back within minutes while known ones wait days. Each deck shows New, Learning and Due counts, with 10 new cards a day by default (adjustable), shuffle, and a weak-cards-only mode.
Progress saves to your account and works offline. Space flips and 1–4 rates on a keyboard; on a phone, tap to flip and swipe left for Again or right for Good.
61 pictures in Identify the Structure that were stored sideways now stand upright, and white borders around the photos are trimmed.

title: Building Laws: DOH Guidelines in Architectural Design
items: New section in Building Laws: DOH Guidelines in Architectural Design, with 15 modules (195 questions), each followed by its own short mixed review (true or false, fill in the blank, matching; 60 questions).

It covers the DOH Permit to Construct rules (AO 2016-0042 and its planning guidelines for hospitals, birthing homes, dialysis clinics, drug rehabilitation centers, drug testing labs and OFW clinics), the 2019 revised checklists, the primary care facility guidelines, and the DOH hospital planning manuals.
Every question names its source (document, annex and item), and some show a plan sketch you can open with Show picture.
The existing Building Laws modules are now grouped: PD 1096, Housing Laws, Mixed Reviews, and Planning & Agencies.

title: Mock board exams: figure questions added
items: The plumbing layout, valves, electrical fittings, slab section and fire alarm riser figures from the mock exams are now attached to their questions. Tap "Show picture" to see them.
Mock Board Exam 1 and 2 now have 895 questions, up from 878.
The five concrete block questions in Mock Exam 2 are left out: the source never printed their figure, and its answer key gives them as free points.

title: Mock board exams: Day 2 design problems and 130 more questions
items: All ten Day 2 design problems are in: each one appears as a scenario above the questions that depend on it, so the setback, footprint, GFA, FLAR and quantity questions can be worked out.
Mock Board Exam 1 and 2 now have 878 questions, up from 748. Repeated questions, questions already in your bank, brand items and items that were garbled or missing in the scan are now included.
The only items still left out are 22 that need a figure (fittings, valves, block types, plan details) or that have no answer key.

title: Mock board exams: 131 more questions and fuller explanations
items: Mock Board Exam 1 and 2 now have 748 questions, up from 617. Questions that were left out only because they couldn't be checked against a code or book are back, with the exam key's answer.

Where the exam explained an answer, that explanation now comes first, followed by a cited law, code or book. Answers taken from the key that couldn't be confirmed start with "Per the exam key", and where a code says something different, the explanation says what the code says.

title: Two full mock board exams in Past Board Exams
items: Past Board Exams has two new groups, Mock Board Exam 1 and Mock Board Exam 2, with 617 questions in 16 modules. Each exam covers Day 1 History, Theory & Professional Practice; Day 1 Utilities, Construction, Structures & Materials; and Day 2 Design, Site Planning & Interiors.

Questions keep their original wording, with only light grammar and scanning fixes, and every explanation ends with a named source such as the NBC IRR, NSCP 2015, the Fire Code RIRR, the amended BP 344 IRR, BP 220 or the 2016 Architect's Guidelines.

Items that needed the exam's drawings or design-problem sheets, picture items, brand questions, and answers that could not be checked against a code or textbook were left out. One answer differs from the exam key: paint's hiding power comes from the pigment, not the "body".

title: Phone reminders now show a question
items: Study and streak reminders on your phone now show a real question from the reviewer instead of a generic nudge. Tap it to answer that question right away.
Admin messages and report replies still show their own text.

title: Building Technology answers checked by a practicing architect
items: Seven more Building Technology refresher questions were added, using an architect's answers: firewall waterproofing, G.I. sheet thickness, G.I. roof leaks, the cheapest and most expensive wash basins, the pivot-door drawback, and dressed lumber size.

Two older drill answers were corrected. Corrugated roofing, not polycarbonate, needs the fewest purlins, and a bi-fold door, not a French door, gives the widest view of a vista. The refresher vista question now answers bi-fold as well.

title: 59 more Building Technology refresher questions
items: The "2027 Refresher – Building Technology" group gained 59 new questions from the November 21 Building Technology refresher (items 1–400). They cover paints and coatings, aggregates and concrete, waterproofing, roofing, glass and glazing, flooring, steel, door hardware, insulation and wood joinery.
Every explanation is written out and ends with a named source, such as ASTM, ACI, NSCP 2015, the Fire Code RIRR, the GANA Glazing Manual or the Wood Handbook.
Items already in the bank, picture-identification slides, brand and price questions, and items with missing choices or no single correct answer were left out.

title: 2,117 new refresher questions in Past Board Exams
items: Past Board Exams has 46 new modules in six '2027 Refresher' groups: Architectural Design & Site Planning, Professional Practice, Structural Conceptualization, Building Utilities, Building Technology, and History & Theory of Architecture.

Each question keeps its original wording, with only light grammar and scanning fixes, and every explanation ends with a named source such as the NBC IRR, NSCP 2015, BP 344, RA 9514, the Plumbing Code or the PEC.

Site-planning scenarios (a lawyer's house, condominiums, a car repair shop, an office condominium, government buildings, a bus terminal, a parking building and a restaurant plaza) show the full project brief above each question.

Picture-identification items were rewritten as text questions where the description was enough. Items with missing choices, unreadable drawings or answers that could not be verified were left out, as were questions already in the bank.

title: Every Past Board Exams explanation rewritten with a source
items: All 3,506 Past Board Exams drill questions now have a fuller explanation that ends with a named source, such as the NBC IRR, NSCP 2015, BP 344 (2024 IRR), RA 9266, the 2016 Architect's Guidelines, the Fire Code RIRR, Fajardo, Ching or UNESCO.
Every mention of a review center, its answer key or its lecturers was removed from the questions and explanations.
Three questions had lost the letter I to scanning errors (such as "I.M. Pei" and "I-beam") and were repaired. The pipe-cover answer now follows NSCP: 40 mm where exposed to earth or weather.
Unit typos in seven questions were fixed (for example, "85 m" now reads "85 cm"), and stray inline choice letters were removed from twelve question stems.

title: Answers checked against your reference files
items: 17 more questions are back, checked against the 2024 BP 344 IRR, the 2016 Architect's Guidelines, OSHS 2019, the NSCP, Fajardo and Time-Saver Standards.

BP 344: accessible stairs 1.50 m wide, handrails on ledges 40 mm clear, vertical door pulls centered at 900 mm. Fees: post-construction 4% to 6% of gross rental; a suspension over 6 months doubles the remaining supervision fee; DAEDS is 7% for a gymnasium and 6% for a supermarket.
PAST BOARD EXAMS Topic Drills now hold 3,506 questions.

title: Awards, records and completed computations
items: 35 more questions are back. Awards and records were checked against PRC, UAP and news sources: the 2022 PRC Outstanding Architect, the Likha Gold Medal awardees, the Eric Nubla award, the Architect's Credo resolutions and the BP 344 bus seats.
Computations that were missing data now state it in the question, then work it out: stair runs, risers, CHB counts, paint, and cement, sand and gravel for Class B and Class C mixes.
PAST BOARD EXAMS Topic Drills now hold 3,489 questions.

title: Answers checked against public sources
items: 31 more questions are back, checked against public sources: architects and buildings (SSS Building, Antipolo Cathedral, the Coconut Palace, the WHO building, SM Megamall, the RONAC Art Center and others), UAP SPP Doc 202 DAEDS fees, and BP 220 / PD 957 lot frontages and motor court widths.
The first president of the Philippine Architects Society is now Juan F. Nakpil, not Tomás Mapúa.
PAST BOARD EXAMS Topic Drills now hold 3,454 questions.

title: More code questions checked against the law text
items: 22 more questions are back, checked against the 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096, the RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR (2019) and the PD 957 IRR: footings, dwelling live loads, wooden posts, view panels, the BHL on narrow roads, subdivision road widths and park allocations.
PAST BOARD EXAMS Topic Drills now hold 3,423 questions.

title: Design Problem computations
items: 65 Design Problem computations are back, worked out step by step from each project brief using the 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (Tables VII.1, VII.2, VII.G.1, VIII.1, VIII.2 and VIII.3, and the firewall rules).
PAST BOARD EXAMS Topic Drills now hold 3,401 questions.

title: Nearly 400 more Topic Drill questions
items: About 360 questions that had been left out as ambiguous or unverified now have answers, each with a short note on why.
28 more picture questions are answered from their figures.
Concrete classes follow Fajardo: Class A is 3,500 psi and Class B is 3,000 psi.
PAST BOARD EXAMS Topic Drills now hold 3,336 questions.

title: History, Theory, Planning and Prof Prac checked against answer keys
items: History, Theory, Planning and Professional Practice answers were checked against reference answer keys; 11 answers were corrected to match.
260 more questions that had been left out are back, keyed from those answer keys.
PAST BOARD EXAMS Topic Drills now hold 2,950 questions.

title: Answers checked against the MST answer keys
items: Building Technology, Building Utilities and Structural answers were checked against reference answer keys, and 34 answers were corrected to match.
About 230 questions that had been left out for unclear answers are back, keyed from the answer keys.
PAST BOARD EXAMS Topic Drills now hold 2,690 questions.

title: Pictures and checked numbers in Topic Drills
items: Topic Drills now include 270 picture questions: tools, hardware, fixtures, trusses, slabs and landmark buildings, each shown with its figure.
About 50 National Building Code and BP 344 number questions are back, checked against the IRR text and updated to the 2024 BP 344 IRR.
Questions whose right answer was missing now have it, and outdated facts are updated (for example, the Sagrada Família is now the tallest church).
Design problems gain area and quantity questions worked out from each project brief.
PAST BOARD EXAMS Topic Drills now hold 2,464 questions.

title: More past board exam practice
items: PAST BOARD EXAMS has 61 new modules of topic drills: 2,086 questions across History, Theory, Planning, Professional Practice, Building Technology, Building Utilities, Structural and Design Problems.
Modules are now grouped: January 2026 Recalls first, then one Topic Drills group per subject.
Design problem questions show the project brief, requirements and site data in the scenario box.

title: Clearer module names and law updates
items: Vague module names now say what is inside, for example "Systems 6 - Fire Suppression & Standpipes" and "Preboard Review - PD 1096, BP 344, RA 9266 & Fire Code".

Updated questions for laws and standards that changed: rebar grades under PNS 49:2020 (280 and 420), the New Government Procurement Act (RA 12009) replacing RA 9184, NEDA becoming DEPDev, HLURB and HUDCC questions marked as pre-2019, and the newer DHSUD minimum floor area for socialized housing, NSO now the PSA, the ERB replaced by the ERC, and the Fire Code's 2019 Revised IRR.

title: Review Drills
items: Practice Sets now ends with Review Drills: 29 topic modules, about 960 questions, rewritten and regrouped by topic from review-center mock sets.

title: Practice Sets
items: New subject: Practice Sets. 247 AI-made drill sets shared by fellow takers, about 12,800 questions, one module per set.
Sets are grouped by topic: history, Filipino architects, building technology, material brands, structural, utilities, laws, professional practice, design problems and past board exam recalls.
The RA 9266 flashcard decks are now multiple-choice, with the other cards' answers as the wrong choices.

title: Fixes from your reports
items: Fixed the questions you reported: wrong answer keys, unclear wording, missing figures and a missing problem statement. Thank you for flagging them.
Checked the whole question bank for the same mistakes and fixed those too, including answers given away by the question itself.
A little coffee cup now peeks from the side of the screen. Tap it to see how to support LEA Reviewer, or hide it for a month.

title: Pop-up quiz
items: Pop-up quiz: open the site and a random question from the whole reviewer pops up. Answer it right and it counts toward your mastery.
A new pop-up quiz question every hour, in the bell and on Home. Pick hourly, or once a day in the morning, at lunch, in the afternoon or in the evening, under Reminders.
Questions with a figure have a Show picture button. Tap the picture to see it full size.
It plays the same sounds as the reviewer: a chime when a card arrives, the right and wrong answer sounds, and a little fanfare for a new mastery. Your volume and mute settings apply.
The board exam countdown now runs to 19 January 2027.

title: Messages
items: Messages got a rebuild: reply to a message, react with an emoji, and @mention someone (or @everyone in Community).
See when someone is typing and when they have seen your message.
A Messages window now opens from the corner of study pages, so you can chat without leaving your review.
Unfinished messages stay put when you switch conversations, and pictures show a preview before you send.
Pop-up notifications are dismissed by swiping them away, sideways or up, instead of hunting for a tiny x.
The site checks for new notifications less often, so it uses less of your data while you review.

title: Chat, member pages and duels
items: Chat: one lobby everyone shares, and private messages to anyone else here. Find it under Account.
Send a picture or a GIF in chat. A big photo is resized for you, and a GIF is turned into a looping clip so it sends quickly.
Tap someone's name to see their page: their rank, how much they have mastered, their average, and whether they are online.
Duels: challenge someone to the same ten questions. You both answer whenever you like, and the result appears once both of you have played.
A duel waiting on you shows up in the bell, with its own filter on the notifications page.
New About page under Account, with how to get in touch.

title: Sound, spoken questions, and a big accuracy sweep
items: Questions can now be read aloud. Tap the speaker on any question.
Sound effects across the site, with volume and mute in Account.
The quiz, Saved, Mnemonics and Reminders now share one exam-booklet page.
New page: Code Plates, the law drawn to scale.
New modules: twelve board-exam recall banks, two Professional Practice refreshers, six Building Technology modules and one Structural module.
New figures for masonry bonds and brick positions, plus every missing or broken picture filled in site-wide.
BP 344 questions now follow the 2024 Revised IRR.
Every PD 1096 and NSCP value was checked against the code itself; the ones that did not match were corrected.
Architectural Design 20 to 24 were rewritten so each question names the law it comes from.
Repeated answer choices removed site-wide, contradicting answers fixed, and reported questions corrected.

title: New app icon
items: LEA Reviewer now has its own logo as the Home Screen app icon.
Already added LEA Reviewer to your Home Screen? Your phone keeps the old icon until you add it again.
Step 1: Open LEA Reviewer in Safari (Chrome on Android) once, so it gets this update.
Step 2: Press and hold the old LEA Reviewer icon on your Home Screen, then tap Remove App (Remove on Android).
Step 3: In Safari, tap Share, then Add to Home Screen. On Android Chrome, tap the ⋮ menu, then Add to Home screen.

title: Study reminders on your phone, and retakes
items: Pick up to six study reminder times a day in Reminders, and get a phone push at each one. Skipped on days you already did the Daily Drill.
A phone push at 8 PM when your streak would end at midnight.
After finishing a module, "Retake the ones you missed" starts a fresh round of just those questions.
The What's New window keeps a fixed size and scrolls inside, so it fits every screen.

title: Phone notifications
items: Turn on phone notifications in Reminders to hear about admin messages and replies to your reports, even when the site is closed.
On iPhone, add LEA Reviewer to your Home Screen first, then turn them on from there.

title: Notifications, reminders and What's New
items: A bell on Home collects messages from the admin, replies to questions you reported, site updates and reminders.
New notifications pop up at the top of the screen, whatever page you are on.
Reminders: Daily Drill nudge, streak at risk, exam countdown, leaderboard rivals, what to study next, and a refresh prompt when a new version is out. Turn each one on or off in Reminders.
Word helper: 28 more word origins in History, plus quick definitions with memory tricks in Structural and Building Utilities. Definitions appear after you answer.
Tapping an underlined word inside an answer no longer picks that answer.
This What's New window, and a Versions tab on your Profile.

title: New subjects and modules
items: New subject: Pritzker Awardees, with six modules.
History of Architecture modules 13 to 17: timeline of styles, movements, isms, Filipino architecture, and the UAP and Filipino architects.
Building Laws module 06: BP 220 housing classifications and site standards.
Mnemonics page with memory hooks from the LEA Discord.
Question banks reworded, and errors fixed in Building Laws and Architectural Design.

title: Fairer question order
items: Questions come in a new order on every attempt.
"All of the above" always stays the last choice.
"Both A and B" choices now point at the right letters after shuffling.

title: Every quiz in the new quiz screen
items: All older quiz pages now open in the same quiz screen, with progress tracking.
Question numbering fixed.
Questions that could not be answered were fixed or hidden.

title: Word origins and scenarios
items: History questions underline key terms: tap one to see where the word comes from.
Situation-based questions show their scenario above the question.
See how other reviewers answered each question.

title: Tidier module lists
items: Modules are listed in their number order.
Long module lists are colour-grouped.
Fixed old copies of pages staying on your device after an update.

title: Weekly standings and clearer questions
items: Weekly standings, counting what you mastered in the last 7 days.
New app icon: a bahay kubo.
Every subject has a short description, and all modules were renamed clearly.
41 questions about figures are back, with newly drawn figures.
Question wording improved in Building Utilities, Building Laws and Structural.

title: The new LEA Reviewer
items: A new quiz screen for every module: study mode, mock exam, and drilling your misses.
New Home with exam countdown, readiness, Daily Drill and streaks.
Results screen showing what you newly mastered.
Desktop layouts for Home and quizzes.
Works offline once a module has been opened.
Profile screen with your own picture, shown on the leaderboard.
Tap a figure to see it full-screen.
Fixes that stop saved progress from being wiped.

title: Pick up where you left off
items: Professional Practice quizzes added.
Resume an unfinished quiz from where you stopped.
Home page and heading fixes.

title: Big redesign
items: New sign-up window and a redesigned look across the site.
See who else is online.
New subject sources, and the TAPP pre-board quiz.

title: Sound and a landing page
items: Sound effects when you answer.
Simple landing page.
Dark theme fixes and more modules.

title: LEA Reviewer launches
items: Quizzes grouped by board exam subject.
Progress saved to your account.
Leaderboard.
